key_insight: K/Rb-based lead-free double perovskites β2SnGeX6 (X = Cl, Br, I) are predicted by DFT to be stable, ductile, and highly tunable semiconductors spanning photovoltaic to thermoelectric applications.
engineering_relevance: The composition-dependent direct bandgap and low lattice thermal conductivity make this family attractive for environmentally benign solar absorbers, tandem/IR devices, and waste-heat recovery materials.
method: DFT-based study of structural, mechanical, electronic, optical, and thermoelectric properties
Calculated formation energies, tolerance factors, and octahedral factors to assess stability
Evaluated elastic constants, band structures, and transport-related metrics including ZT
evidence_signal: The abstract reports cubic structural stability across all six compounds, direct bandgaps tunable from 1.44 to 0.64 eV, and a peak thermoelectric performance of ZT = 2.4 for K2SnGeI6 at 1000 K.
watch_item: The most impressive thermoelectric performance is predicted at high temperature and from first-principles calculations, so experimental validation of phase stability, defect tolerance, and synthesis quality is still needed.
paper_title: First-Principles Study of Novel Lead-Free Double Perovskite \b{eta}2SnGeX6 (\b{eta} = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) for thermomechanical, optoelectronic and outstanding thermoelectric applications
